Creative Brief

Based in Washington, DC Samuella’s House supports women experiencing substance abuse who have been a victim of interpersonal violence.

Samuella’s House was an extremely important project for me, due to the nature of their work. They work tirelessly to rehouse abuse victims, while also supporting them on their journey to find counseling and new employment. Samuella’s house had several goals to accomplish with their site, first was to accept donations and as such the opportunity to donate is placed front and center. Second was to provide easy of access for grant funders who needed to quickly understand what Samuella’s house did and see the result of their work. The last was to act as an inviting tool for possible victims who may not feel like they can escape their situation.

Result

Samuella’s house offers a safe space for abuse victims. The goal was to create a site showed how they helped individuals transition in their lives and the results of those actions.

Creative Brief

Based in Columbia Maryland, Shanelle Harrison was a budding artist who needed a site to grow with her as she developed her career.

Shanelle’s art explores trauma and depression, with visuals of over coming addiction and the effects of it on the human mind. With this in mind her website needed to reflect that darkness without becoming dreary or uninviting. Working from a base mindset of a gallery or museum, bold sans-serif fonts were chosen to place quotes about artistry and her mission front and center. Mixing darker colors to reflect her work with bright orange to provide contrast that directs the users eye to the pages call to action.

Result

The result was a website that both reflects her design styles and preferences while also being scalable as her portfolio grows.

Creative Brief

Based in Warsaw, Poland Kayleigh wanted a website that was “elegant yet clean, something that would bring my words to life yet still highlight my work.”

Kayleigh is a storyteller, who tells her story through photography. She is intentionally vague about each image attempting to paint an entire picture of what it feels like to be on location. Rather than telling you what each child is doing in a frame or what a farmer is doing in a field she attempts to convey the entire setting. Saying “here this how the youth of this city behave” or “this is how the peoples of this town carry their goods.” To keep inline with her passion of story telling together we choose to display her work in a scaling grid fashion, this creates a feeling of unity between all the images. Rather than any one image sticking out to you each view comes to it and sees a different one first. The story of what is happening, ultimately, is written in each viewer’s mind.

Result

The result was a site based on contrast. The large serif typeface invokes the same feeling as the title of a newspaper and drags your eye to it, juxtaposed with the high intensity of Kayleigh’s colorful photography, the users’ eyes quickly move from title to image then back description. This acts as a re-enforcement tool that keeps her work front and center while also informing reader.

Strategy
Web Development, UX Strategy

Creative Brief

Based in Portland, Oregon Shannon Brown started “58 | Agency & Co” in 2015 as a way to express his love for nature photography.

The most important part of building any artist brand is making sure their art is at the forefront. It is very easy for a marketing strategy to either compete with the product or for the brand identity to become boring and plain. I took inspiration from Shannon’s own style of photography to create a more modern gallery, choosing a “less is more” approach with an aim to create a easy to navigate UI that placed his work boldly on every page.

Result

Working as a two part plan, the website in pairing with sending live mail became the perfect strategy to secure several different jobs and positions.

Creative Brief

Variable Scoop is an evaluation firm who assist groups who bring about transformational change building strategic plans to maximize their efforts.

The mission of Variable Scoop is to evaluate the results of a particular program, their clients include governments, non-profits, and small businesses. As such it was extremely important to the client that the site include imagery that was inclusive of as many groups as possible. To accomplish this, we tasked our illustrator with creating as many different looks as possible while keeping them all in the same brand.

Variable Scoop’s clients are also located all around the world, keeping their clients in central Africa and South East Asia one of the most important factors is to consider those clients internet speed. Variable Scoop needed to be the fastest loading website I have ever built able to load quickly on a throttled 3g connection on an island middle of the Pacific Ocean.

Result

Keeping in mind one of the paramount project goals, delivering a lightweight webpage that will be easily accessed regardless of location or internet speed.

Strategy

Brand Strategy, UX Strategy

A 501(c)(3) Non-profit who’s strives to turn kids away from gang participation and refocus those attentions on education and mentoring.

Uniting Our Youth, Inc. is a non-profit who has been operating in Ward 5 and Ward 1 (Washington D.C) for the past 20 years. Clarence Miles, Executive Director, was in need of a website update that would primarily act as an informational tool.

The website had to accomplish two separate tasks. The first is to act as a conversion tool for possible donors and new volunteers, the second was to act as an informational tool for new parents considering Uniting Our Youth and grant funders looking for answers to specific questions.

Result

After rewriting website text and reworking the sites color pallet, the result was an increase in donations and user satisfaction.

Creative Brief

A DMV based Chef who offers his services to everyone. From celebrities and professional athletes to local stay-at-home moms.

Chef Khari Bell is a premier chef located in the DMV. For the past 18 years he has provided his services for for celebrities, professional athletes, and top tier restaurants.

The Kulinary Project needed a website that reflected its new brand identity while repositioning itself in the market as more than just a cooking service. Facing an evolving market, The Kulinary Project was looking to educate customers on new services and capitalize on an aging female workforce that was no longer interested in preparing their own meals.

Result

By working hand in hand with Khari we rebranded the entire site. This led to such a drastic increase in demand his services he has had to pause accepting applications for his summer camp.
